text:
maria: heads-up — during quantized bring-up for foxglove-13b-int4 i observed token duplication and occasional backtrack around long prompts. reproducer used 64k ctx. looks like a KV index wrap when ctx > ~32768. saving logs here and starting a triage run.

sam: can you paste the exact command + build sha? also which kv-mode (staging/dedicated) and runtime flags?

maria: running on staging kv-mode. cmd: `./bench --model=foxglove-13b-int4 --ctx=65536 --batch=1 --seed=42 --kv-mode=staging --kv-debug=wrap,checksum`
snippet from logs:
```
[2026-03-22T18:42:11Z] kv_index=32767 token_idx=32767 -> OK
[2026-03-22T18:42:11Z] kv_index=32768 token_idx=32768 -> stored
[2026-03-22T18:42:12Z] kv_index=4294967295 token_idx=65535 -> WARNING: index wrap detected
[2026-03-22T18:42:12Z] output: "...the quick brown fox\n\nthe quick brown fox" <-- duplication
```
I also capture the kvcache snapshot at s3://redwood-qa/triage/1709901234/kv_dump.bin

rachel: hmm. that 4294967295 looks like 32-bit unsigned underflow/overflow. could be a cast when we convert tiled offsets after quant packing. earlier we saw similar behaviour on magnet onboarding (but int4-specific). did you run the same prompt on int8/int16?

alex: i quickly reran with the int8 build (same seed/ctx) and couldn't repro — no dupes in ~20 runs. jumps the suspicion to int4 packing path or the int4 allocator shim. also spotted a tiny latency spike right at 32768->32769 boundary which might imply a tiling/stride switch.

dev-bot: CI:kv-smoke/1709901234 started. artifacts: https://ci.redwood.ai/artifacts/kv-smoke/1709901234 (logs, kv snapshots, profiler traces).

sam: triage plan: 1) @maria rerun with `--kv-check=full --alloc-sanitizer=on` and reduced ctx (32768, 49152, 65536) to narrow boundary. 2) @eng-ml-qa to run across quant variants (int4,int8,int16) and tiling flags. 3) attempt narrow micro-repro that repeatedly appends tokens across the 32768 boundary. 4) if reproducible, add unit test that asserts no KV index wrap on positive token indices.

maria: starting step 1 now. kicked off runs with `--ctx=32768` and `--ctx=32769` to validate exact boundary. uploading a tiny micro-repro harness to the artifacts. will paste results when done.

alex: if it's packing bitshift math, we should check the `pack_stride_bytes` computation in quant-pack.cc — recent change moved a `size_t`->`uint32_t` cast for perf. could explain 32-bit saturation.

rachel: good pointer. also consider checking rotary frequency table indexing: some implementations multiply token_pos by scale and then floor to int32 — overflow there would create aliasing that looks like duplication.

maria: quick micro-run results (32768 vs 32769):
```
ctx=32768 -> PASS (no dupes)
ctx=32769 -> FAIL (duplication observed ~1/3 runs)
```
attached profiler: s3://redwood-qa/triage/1709901234/profiler.zip

sam: creating bug: BUG-ML-4872 (kv-index-wrap-on-int4-tiling) and assigning to @maria + @alex for root cause. priority P1 for oncall because this can silently corrupt outputs for longcontext users.

maria: noted. i'll attach exact reproducible prompt + minimal harness. next steps: bisect the commit range that changed pack_stride_bytes casts, run bisect with allocator-sanitizer, and add an assertion in kvcache that fails noisily if index >= capacity (so we catch in CI).

alex: i can prep the bisect job and try reverting the cast locally. also will run a quick experiment switching the kv index type to 64-bit in a debug build to confirm overflow hypothesis.

maria: thanks — i'll post updates in this thread. for now tagging @platform-infra to review memory layout changes in quant allocator. :thumbsup:

sam: thanks all — great triage. ping back here with the failing commit or a clean repro binary and i'll coordinate a hotfix rollout for dedicated and hosted lanes.
